touches.text: QUESTIONS: a question is [Q#n: ...], placed at the line it bears on. Its #n is its own and never changes; a new one takes the next unused number, which is now 127. An answered question disappears: its answer is folded into the intention and why (0.2.1), and signed where it records a decision (0.5). Why? Becuase too many words makes it hard for both akien and Claude to understand.

A choice CC can answer is not a question; it is a hypothesis. The ticket carries CC's answer as its hypothesis, and its WATCHME feeds the hypothesis back to cc_0 with enough data to review it and rewrite it as we learn. The notation carries the question: a HYPOTHESIS asks whether it works, or is faster, or whatever it claims, and the WATCHME answers that. A question asks only what Akien alone can settle. Why? Because a question with a recommendation asks him to adjudicate what a measurement can settle. This holds everywhere. - CC
Questions live here and nowhere else. The questions/ inbox and `cairn question` are deprecated for now. -amm

The abstract ticket owns what every kind shares: its birth (cast) and its three parts, each with one job: the plan (only what a builder builds from), the metadata and state (what gates and doors read and write as it moves), and the history (the append-only log). WHY: one job per part reduces confusion; a builder reads the plan and nothing else.

Outline check: when a ticket is cast, the cheapest model reads it beside the outline sections it touches. A conflict, or an open question in those sections, becomes a [Q#n] at the outline line it bears on (0.6.2), and that open [Q#n] holds the ticket's build until it is answered. It reads the outline as it stands each time, so editing the outline costs nothing. WHY: a ticket that contradicts the outline builds something Akien did not intend, and the cheapest time to catch that is before the build. - CC

A ticket's plan carries only what a door can check. A decision line's by (free prose on every ticket) is not checked and not kept: the cast door checks writes_to and reads, and by goes. Who authored a line is not tracked, except on a gate-pass certificate. WHY: tickets moved from prose to JSON so their contents can be checked; a field no door checks is prose. - CC

Reds don't get lost. Each run writes a ticket for every new red it finds and every orphaned file it sees, unless one is already open for it. A red seen in passing gets the same treatment. Every red and every orphaned file is fixed; one unrelated to the work in hand is ticketed, and once it is, that crossing can go ahead.

A red is first a question: is the code wrong, or is the tooth measuring the wrong thing? An LLM reads the work against the component's why, the tooth's why and CP1-CP6, because even the Laws rest finally on the core principles. Either the code or the tooth changes, and a tooth change carries that decision in the same act (corrosion, 17.11.6). A tooth a hollow build could pass is worthless at every tier (Law 8).

outline_check: the outline check of 9.3.5.1. It reads one ticket beside the outline as it stands, and each conflict, or open question in a section the ticket touches, holds the ticket's build until answered. WHY: a ticket filed without anyone reading the outline should not reach a build unnoticed. - CC

question: the open-question door: a decision only the operator can make, bound to its ticket, answered in the operator's words. WHY: a spec choice is settled by Akien's head, recorded verbatim, never by a paragraph of CC's. USERS: tickets and CodeMother open them; the operator answers (7.4.2).

RULE 1, ENCAPSULATION: every component talks to every other only through that component's public interface: a device's is the bus plus any client tool it publishes; a machine's or tool's is what its entry declares. Nothing outside a device reaches into its code, skills included. A ticket builds inside its own component, and its proofs measure only that component. WHY: it limits a change to the component that made it.
SIGNING: where a decision must be recorded, the line ends with a by-line naming who made the call. Lines with no decision in them carry none. Why? So we know who to ask first when adjudicating.
When two gates conflict, check each gate's teeth against its why and drop the ones that no longer hold. That is why every gate carries a why. -amm
